target_customer: Software engineering teams at companies of all sizes that need internal tools such as admin panels and dashboards
problem: Engineers spent weeks building repetitive internal tools made of tables, buttons and forms.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat plus self-hosted enterprise plans
product_category: Low-code internal tools platform for developers

founders.name: David Hsu
education: University of Oxford, studied philosophy and computer science, graduated before launching Cashew (Sequoia profile)
previous_startups: Cashew, a peer-to-peer payments startup accepted into Y Combinator
founders.background_notes: Pivoted from Cashew to Retool about 60 days before YC Demo Day after realizing the internal tools he built were the market, per secondary write ups. No prior employer is named in the Sequoia profile or on the YC page.

investors: founders of GitHub, Gusto, PagerDuty, Plaid, Segment, Stripe and Y Combinator

technical_complexity.rationale: A drag and drop builder connected to arbitrary databases and APIs is standard but broad engineering; permissions, hosting and reliability grew harder with scale.

defensibility.rationale: Apps built in the tool are tied to its components and data connections, and developer word of mouth built a base, but open source rivals and in-house builds were possible.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought or neutralized Retool as of the sources read; it grew to a 3.2B USD valuation in 2022 and remained independent.

market_need_then: Developer time spent on internal tools was widely felt; Retool reportedly reached about 2M USD ARR before its public launch in August 2018 (First Round interview, secondary summary).

identity.logo: Block style R mark per secondary sources, with a refreshed combination mark in a 2024 rebrand; sources conflict on the details
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and developer first; recent copy plays on vibe coding and governance

rebrands.why: Not stated; date and details come from weak secondary sites

branding.community_and_virality: Founder interviews on Changelog, Acquired and First Round, and a developer community; no merch evidence verified.

brand_strength.rationale: Well known among developers through podcasts and word of mouth, but sources about the brand design itself are weak.

pivots.why: The internal tools Hsu built for fraud detection and compliance revealed a larger underserved market (secondary sources)

outcome_analysis: Retool pivoted from a failing fintech to an internal tools builder during YC and reached early revenue through developer led sales. It raised a Sequoia led Series A (amount and date not confirmed by a primary source), a 50M USD Series B at 925M USD on 2020-10-20, a 20M USD Series C at 1.85B USD on 2021-12-22 and a 45M USD extension at 3.2B USD in July 2022. Layoffs of about 30 people in June 2023 are listed by one aggregator. It remains independent and is repositioning toward AI app building.
notes: Series A: the Sequoia profile says Bryan Schreier led it, but no source opened here gives its date or amount (aggregators say 25M USD in 2019, with conflicting months, and a Bloomberg snippet mentions an earlier 25M USD round; Bloomberg returned 403 and was not worked around), so date and amount are null. The July 2022 round was announced as Series C2 by the company press release per search results, so it is recorded as other rather than a new letter stage. Series B: Retool blog and SiliconANGLE agree on date, amount, valuation. SiliconANGLE states total raised 75M USD after the Series B. Dec 2021 valuation: SiliconANGLE says 1.85B USD, a Forbes headline says 1.9B USD; 1.85B used. A 1M USD seed (September 2017) appears only on aggregators and is not recorded. Valuation conflict July 2022: Techzine headline 3.4B, body and TechCrunch headline 3.2B. The TechCrunch July 2022 URL returned 404 earlier. No dated 2017 competitor source was found, so the list is empty. The layoff figure comes from TrueUp, an aggregator. Oxford education and Cashew description come from the Sequoia profile; the earlier claim that Cashew was a UK fintech that failed is removed as uncited.
